findings.evidence: The candidate head is 49318c6, and its task-content digest is 23b1a4ba.... The committed independent-review-request.json (candidate.diff:300-385) and both reports show candidate_head b1cd2f3 and task_content digest eed35b4d.... automated-checks.json records head b1cd2f3 and digest d01844a0.... verification.md 'Post-archive integration fix' (candidate.diff:694) says the review was rerun on the archived change and that 'the committed reports and automated-checks.json are those runs'. Only the request and spec-fidelity.json are modified in the working tree (uncommitted), and engineering-quality.json is not. So the candidate as committed contradicts its own receipt, and finish's require_publication_review_evidence would see a digest mismatch unless the refreshed files are committed first.
findings.summary: The review evidence in the candidate tree binds to an earlier commit than the candidate head, and verification.md's claim that the committed reports are the post-fix reruns does not match it.

findings.evidence: independent_review.record_report rejects reports with reviewer.launch_evidence == PLATFORM_OBSERVED (candidate.diff:1633-1637). Nothing binds a report to the runner beyond that string and an output_sha256 of data the same file holds. A hand-written file placed in independent-reviews/ with launch_evidence 'platform-observed' and a matching request_id and digest would satisfy validate_evidence. The evidence_matches_checkout change also accepts any content under independent-reviews/ (openspec_lifecycle.py, _is_review_evidence). This is 'mandatory' only against accidental omission, not against fabrication, so the docs should not describe it as proof.
findings.summary: The 'platform-observed' launch proof is a plain string in a JSON report that any writer can produce. Only the `record` CLI refuses it.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/independent_review_runner.py: after communicate() returns normally, `_kill_process_group(process)` runs os.killpg(process.pid, SIGKILL) unconditionally, and ProcessLookupError and PermissionError are swallowed. Once the leader is reaped, its pgid can be reused by an unrelated group leader.
findings.summary: subprocess_launcher unconditionally SIGKILLs the process group after the reviewer has exited and been reaped, so a reused PID could take the signal.

findings.evidence: claude_argv uses `--tools Read,Grep,Glob --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <scratch>`, and codex uses `--sandbox read-only`. Both can read arbitrary local files. parse_findings stores the `evidence` strings as returned, and run_review writes them to independent-reviews/*.json, which are committed with the archive.
findings.summary: The read-only guarantee covers writes only. The reviewer's read tools are not confined to the repository, and finding evidence is persisted verbatim in committed reports.

findings.evidence: task_content_identity.py review_exclusion: `archived = any((root/'openspec'/'changes'/'archive').glob(f"*-{change}")) and not (root/active).is_dir()`. Any archive directory ending in `-<change>` matches, unlike independent_review.resolve_change, which uses canonical_change_name.
findings.summary: review_exclusion decides that a change is archived with a loose suffix glob that is inconsistent with the canonical-name check used elsewhere.

findings.evidence: independent_review_runner.workspaces() returns [root, integration_root(root)], and _mutations() reports any change in either. run_perspective turns that into an 'unavailable' report saying the reviewer mutated the workspace. ensure_review_evidence reruns on unavailable-only state, so archive can repeatedly fail or re-launch while another task writes to the integration checkout. AGENTS.md says that state belongs to other agents.
findings.summary: The read-only postcheck snapshots the shared integration checkout, so legitimate concurrent work by another agent marks the review unavailable, and each retry costs two full launches.
